title: Insalata di Polpo
subtitle: Italian octopus salad with lemon, celery, and olive oil
excerpt: Insalata di polpo is a southern Italian salad of tender octopus dressed with lemon juice, celery, olive oil, and parsley. The octopus is simmered slowly until it is firm but yielding, then cooled and sliced while still warm so it absorbs the dressing. Serve chilled or at room temperature.
sourceNotes: Octopus salad is a standard antipasto across the coastal regions of southern Italy, particularly in Puglia, Campania, Calabria, and Sicily. Octopus is widely consumed in all these regions and the cool, lemon-dressed salad is the classic way to serve it as a starter. The dish appears in regional cookbooks from Pellegrino Artusi onward and is found on virtually every seafood restaurant menu in southern Italy.

recipe.batchNotes: Makes well in a double batch. Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the full salad up to a day ahead. The flavour improves after a few hours as the dressing is absorbed.

glossaryTerms.definition: Octopus is tender when a knife slides into the thickest part of the tentacle with no resistance. This takes 45 to 60 minutes for a 1 kg octopus. Overcooked octopus is rubbery; undercooked is tough in a different way.

content.text: Insalata di polpo is poached octopus, sliced while warm, and dressed with lemon juice, olive oil, celery, and parsley. The octopus needs an hour of slow poaching to become

. Dressed while warm, it absorbs the lemon and oil into the flesh rather than just coating the surface. Served at room temperature or chilled, it is one of the most refreshing summer starters in Italian cooking.

items.prepNote: crushed and peeled, for the cooking water

content.text: Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the bay leaves and garlic if using. Do not add salt.

Lower the octopus into the water, head first. The tentacles will curl up immediately. Reduce to a steady simmer and cook for 45 to 60 minutes until a knife slides into the thickest part of a tentacle with no resistance.
Remove the octopus from the water and leave to cool for 10 minutes. While still warm, cut the tentacles into 2 to 3 cm pieces and the body into thick strips.
Place the warm octopus in a bowl. Add the celery, parsley, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Toss well.
Leave to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Serve cold or at room temperature, drizzled with a little more olive oil.

Octopus salad is eaten throughout southern Italy and Sicily, wherever octopus is landed and sold. In Puglia, it is served at the start of seafood meals and eaten in large quantities at Christmas. In Naples, polpi verace (true octopus) are a street food, boiled in a large pot and eaten with lemon directly from the paper. The salad version is a step up from the street version: the same octopus, dressed more carefully and served cooled.
